skill.name: biomni
skill.description: Autonomous biomedical AI agent framework for executing complex research tasks across genomics, drug discovery, molecular biology, and clinical analysis. Use this skill when conducting multi-step biomedical research including CRISPR screening design, single-cell RNA-seq analysis, ADMET prediction, GWAS interpretation, rare disease diagnosis, or lab protocol optimization. Leverages LLM reasoning with code execution and integrated biomedical databases.
skill.summary: Use Biomni to plan, run, and document multi-step biomedical research analyses.
skill.author: davila7

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are documentation-only examples, markdown code fences, printed URLs, or benign formatting and were adjudicated as false positives. Real risks remain in the setup helper credential flow, selected subprocess and file-write paths, troubleshooting guidance that prints API keys, unrestricted generated-code execution, and unescaped HTML report rendering.

remediation.issue: Biomni can execute LLM-generated code with full system privileges.
remediation.suggestion: Make sandboxed execution the default, document isolation requirements before task examples, and warn users before enabling unrestricted execution.

remediation.issue: The setup script stores API keys in plaintext .env files and can print shell export lines.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer a secret manager or masked prompts, set restrictive file permissions, and never display full secret values.

remediation.issue: The setup script writes and runs local helper files.
remediation.suggestion: Check for existing filenames before writing, show the exact command before subprocess execution, and require explicit confirmation.

remediation.issue: The report generator renders conversation content as HTML without escaping.
remediation.suggestion: Escape all user and assistant content before HTML rendering or use a vetted markdown sanitizer.

semantic_findings.title: Unrestricted Generated Code Execution
semantic_findings.description: The skill documents that Biomni executes LLM-generated code with full system privileges and recommends isolation for production use. This is a high-impact capability if used with sensitive data or untrusted prompts.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The documentation directly states full-privilege generated-code execution, and the API reference shows code execution enabled with sandbox mode disabled by default.

semantic_findings.title: Unescaped HTML Report Rendering
semantic_findings.description: The report generator inserts conversation content into HTML without escaping. A malicious conversation history could place active HTML or script content in a generated report.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The converter wraps raw message lines in HTML tags and the template embeds the converted output directly. I found no escaping step before writing HTML reports.

high_findings.confidence_reasoning: The documentation directly states full-privilege generated-code execution, and the API reference shows code execution enabled with sandbox mode disabled by default.

medium_findings.title: Python file write/append
medium_findings.confidence_reasoning: The script writes a generated test_biomni.py file in the current directory. This can overwrite a local file and is later executed by the setup workflow.

medium_findings.title: Python file write/append
medium_findings.confidence_reasoning: The script writes an example_biomni_usage.py file in the current directory. This is a user-visible filesystem side effect and can overwrite an existing file.

medium_findings.title: Unescaped HTML Report Rendering
medium_findings.description: The report generator inserts conversation content into HTML without escaping. A malicious conversation history could place active HTML or script content in a generated report.
medium_findings.confidence_reasoning: The converter wraps raw message lines in HTML tags and the template embeds the converted output directly. I found no escaping step before writing HTML reports.

content.value_statement: Biomedical research tasks often span many data sources, tools, and analysis steps. Biomni helps plan, execute, and document multi-step analyses across genomics, drug discovery, and clinical research.
actual_capabilities: Guides Biomni installation and LLM provider configuration.
Shows how to initialize A1 agents and run natural language biomedical tasks.
Provides examples for CRISPR screens, single-cell RNA-seq, ADMET, GWAS, and clinical genomics.
Documents setup for Claude, OpenAI, Azure OpenAI, Gemini, Groq, AWS Bedrock, and custom endpoints.
Includes helper scripts for environment setup and conversation report generation.
Explains MCP integration for external biomedical APIs and search tools.
limitations: Requires the Biomni package, API keys, compute resources, and a large data download.
Biomni may execute generated code, so sensitive work needs isolation.
Scientific and clinical outputs need expert review before use.
Setup scripts write local files and should be reviewed before running.

use_cases.title: Plan CRISPR Screens
use_cases.description: Design gene prioritization, screening criteria, and expected pathway hits for a research phenotype.

use_cases.title: Analyze Single-Cell Data
use_cases.description: Structure quality control, clustering, cell annotation, and differential expression work for RNA-seq studies.

use_cases.title: Interpret Biomedical Evidence
use_cases.description: Combine variants, pathways, literature, and clinical databases into a reproducible research summary.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Gene Query
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Biomni to summarize the known functions of TP53. Include major pathways, disease links, and important caveats.

prompt_templates.title: Design a CRISPR Screen
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Biomni to design a CRISPR knockout screen for autophagy regulators in HEK293 cells. Include prioritization criteria and controls.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze Single-Cell RNA-seq
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Biomni to plan analysis for a single-cell RNA-seq study. Cover quality control, clustering, annotation, and differential expression.

prompt_templates.title: Run Cross-Domain Interpretation
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Biomni to interpret GWAS hits for a disease. Map variants to genes, run pathway enrichment, and identify follow-up experiments.

output_examples.input: Design a CRISPR screen for genes that regulate autophagy in HEK293 cells.
output_examples.output: A structured screen plan with candidate pathways, control groups, prioritization rules, and validation experiments.

output_examples.input: Analyze a single-cell RNA-seq dataset from treated and untreated samples.
output_examples.output: An analysis outline covering quality filters, clustering strategy, marker review, condition comparison, and interpretation steps.

output_examples.input: Interpret GWAS results for a disease trait and suggest follow-up work.
output_examples.output: A research summary with significant loci, candidate genes, enriched pathways, evidence strength, and experimental next steps.

best_practices: Run Biomni in an isolated environment before using sensitive data.
Review generated code and data paths before execution.
Save reports with task context, data sources, assumptions, and expert review notes.
anti_patterns: Do not treat Biomni output as clinical advice without qualified review.
Do not expose production API keys or patient data to generated code.
Do not run helper scripts before reading their file writes and subprocess calls.

faq.question: What does this skill help me do?
faq.answer: It helps use Biomni for multi-step biomedical research tasks across genomics, drug discovery, and clinical analysis.

faq.question: Does it install Biomni automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides setup guidance and helper scripts that users must review and run themselves.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Can it work without API keys?
faq.answer: Most Biomni workflows need at least one configured LLM provider key.

faq.question: Is Biomni safe for sensitive data?
faq.answer: Use isolation and expert controls. The documentation states that Biomni can execute generated code with full privileges.

faq.question: Can I use outputs for clinical decisions?
faq.answer: No. Treat outputs as research assistance and require qualified scientific or clinical review.
